transcript: Some people reach a point where happiness doesn't feel real anymore. It feels distant, muted, or almost impossible to access. They laugh, smile, and act cheerful around others, not because they feel joy, but because pretending is easier than explaining the emptiness inside. Over time, numbness becomes their default state, not sad, not happy, just nothing. For many, this emotional numbness forms as a defense mechanism. After dealing with repeated disappointment, heartbreak, or emotional overload, the mind starts protecting itself by shutting down feelings all, all together. Happiness begins to feel unfamiliar, like something meant for everyone else but them. So they learn to perform happiness instead, to avoid questions, to fit in, to not ruin the mood, or simply because they don't want to burden anyone with what's really going on. And what people often don't see is how exhausting it is to constantly act okay. Some people aren't cold or emotionless, they're just tired of feeling too much. So now they feel nothing at all. If this feels like you, you don't have to carry it alone. Inside the inner circle, we don't pretend to be okay. We learn how to feel again, gently. The link is in my profile.
